overview:
Techspert is the world's first AI-driven expert network, founded in 2016 by Graham Mills and David Holden-White in Cambridge, UK. The company's core innovation is its deep search technology — machine learning algorithms that autonomously crawl online content in real time to identify the most qualified expert for any topic, no matter how niche. The platform can review profiles of 150 million potential experts from academic journals, medical registries, patent databases, and biographical data in minutes.

Techspert has carved out a strong position in healthcare and life sciences, where finding experts in highly specialized therapeutic areas, rare diseases, and cutting-edge research requires searching beyond traditional expert databases. The company positions itself as a global leader in healthcare and life sciences expert connections, complementing its AI-driven sourcing with a growing international team in Cambridge and Houston.

The company has raised approximately £13.5 million across three funding rounds, backed by investors including BGF, Nauta Capital, Cambridge Angels, and Angel CoFund. Techspert has delivered projects in 100+ geographies, demonstrating the global reach of its AI-powered expert discovery engine.

history.narrative:
Graham Mills and David Holden-White founded Techspert (originally as techspert.io) in 2016 in Cambridge, UK. Both founders had previously co-founded a biotech startup focused on reducing nicotine addiction, which gave them firsthand experience with the difficulty of finding niche scientific experts. David holds a Master's in Biochemistry from Oxford and a Master's in Bioscience Enterprise from Cambridge.

The company raised £1 million in its first funding round in December 2018 from angel investors including Simon Thorpe, Angel CoFund, John Spearman, and GW Asia Capital. In February 2020, Techspert closed a £3.75 million Series A led by pan-European VC Nauta Capital. The company's biggest round came in October 2021: £8.8 million ($12M) from BGF and Nauta Capital, which funded international expansion including the opening of a Houston, Texas office.

aiPlatform.narrative: Techspert's technology is its core competitive advantage. Co-founder Graham Mills describes the platform: 'Our platform scrapes the entirety of public information accessible via semantic web searching' — including academic journals, medical registries, and biographical data. The NLP engine processes this unstructured data to build dynamic expert profiles, then uses ML matching algorithms to rank candidates by relevance to a given brief. Unlike traditional expert networks that rely on opt-in databases of registered experts, Techspert can find professionals who have never signed up for any expert network, dramatically expanding the searchable universe to 150 million+ individuals.

complianceExtended.narrative: Techspert maintains standard compliance protocols appropriate for its focus on technical and scientific consultations. The company's AI-assisted credential verification cross-references expert qualifications against public databases, adding a layer of automated validation on top of manual review. As a UK-based company, Techspert operates under GDPR requirements for data handling of the professional profiles it processes.

Conflict-of-interest screening integrated into expert matching workflow
complianceExtended.regulatoryContext: Techspert's primary focus on healthcare and life sciences consultations — rather than investment research — means it operates with somewhat different compliance requirements than finance-focused expert networks. The company's processing of 150M+ professional profiles requires careful GDPR compliance for data collection and retention. Clean regulatory record.

clientFit.narrative: Techspert is purpose-built for clients who need to find niche technical and scientific experts that traditional expert networks cannot source. The platform excels when the required expertise is highly specialized — rare diseases, emerging technologies, regulatory science — and the experts are not registered on any database. Clients seeking general business expertise or high-volume, routine expert calls may find traditional networks more efficient.
